title: Your fridge is heating your kitchen

beats.text: Your fridge makes your kitchen hotter.
Sounds wrong? Then build one yourself.
You want to keep food cold. So you put it in a box.
But heat always flows from hot to cold. Right through the walls.
So you insulate the walls. That slows the heat down. But it doesn't stop it.
What really cools things down is evaporation. That's why you shiver when you step out of a pool.
So you run a pipe through the box. Inside it, a liquid that boils far below freezing.
It sucks the heat right out of your food. That's the evaporator.
But now the pipe is full of warm gas.
So a pump squeezes that gas together. Squeezed gas gets hot. Hotter than your kitchen. That's the compressor.
A grid on the back dumps that heat into your kitchen. The gas turns back into a liquid. That's the condenser.
Then a super thin tube drops the pressure. The liquid turns ice cold.
And the whole loop starts over.
Congrats. You just built a fridge.
But it doesn't make cold. It just shovels heat from the inside to the back. Plus the heat from the motor.
So leaving the fridge door open won't cool your kitchen.
